If the prompt is unavailable, aborted, or fails—or if persistence or policy
re-evaluation fails—the checkpoint queue remains held while the user's normal
branch push continues. Accessible mode must use a supported explicit selection
path or hold; it must never accept a default implicitly, panic, or consume
pre-push stdin. The held message remains actionable and points to `entire trust`
and the resolved settings file.

Every checkpoint-egress entry point consumes the same `RepoPolicy` decision.
Doctor or another explicitly invoked maintenance path does not bypass the trust
gate merely because it is interactive.

## Agent hook model

Each supported agent has one declarative hook specification that drives:

- installation;
- recognition and version checks;
- deduplication between user and repository scope;
- removal of stale Entire entries;
- expected counts; and
- doctor/status completeness reporting.

The declarative specification preserves the complete existing event set and
command behavior. In particular, Gemini continues installing all twelve current
entries: `SessionStart`, both `SessionEnd` matchers, `BeforeAgent`, `AfterAgent`,
`BeforeModel`, `AfterModel`, `BeforeToolSelection`, `BeforeTool`, `AfterTool`,
`PreCompress`, and `Notification`. Events that currently parse to no lifecycle
event remain installed because their presence is part of the supported Gemini
integration contract. Claude Code likewise preserves its current lifecycle and
tool-use matcher coverage: `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`, `Stop`, `SubagentStop`,
`UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse[Agent]`, `PostToolUse[Agent]`, and
`PostToolUse[TaskCreate|TaskUpdate]`. The refactor deduplicates how these entries
are declared and reconciled; it does not prune or reinterpret them.
Legacy user/repository hook forms are normalized during foreground
reconciliation so correctness does not depend on byte-identical historical
commands.

An agent-hook process resolves `RepoPolicy` once. Root pre-run, hook dispatch,
lazy setup, logging, and lifecycle code reuse that snapshot rather than reloading
settings or re-running Git probes.

### Hook reconciliation operations

User-scope reconciliation runs only from these integration-changing entry
points:

- supported installer/post-install integrations, including
  `curl-bash-post-install`;
- `entire enable`;
- `entire agent add`; and
- doctor's confirmed repair path.

It does not run from hooks or read-only commands such as `status`, `help`,
`version`, `auth token`, or JSON inspection commands. Reconciliation targets
only supported agents positively detected as installed, or agents whose user
configuration already contains an Entire entry. It modifies user-scope config
only. Repository-scope legacy normalization occurs only during an explicit
repo-mutating `enable`, `configure`, or confirmed doctor repair.

Each agent config uses a bounded per-file lock and an atomic, lossless
read-modify-write that preserves non-Entire entries. Installer and ordinary
enable paths report a warning and continue if user-hook reconciliation fails;
doctor reports an unresolved repair. Recursion suppression prevents a hook
process or a child Entire invocation from entering reconciliation.

Lazy per-clone Git setup uses a versioned component record derived from the
current Git-hook and checkpoint-ref specifications, replacing the stale
`GlobalSetupCompleted` boolean. A hook reruns only missing/outdated components;
doctor reports the same component state and does not need to clear a latch to
make a later hook repair it.

## Status, doctor, and errors

Status reports:

- whether global tracking is configured and enabled;
- the resolved settings-file path;
- activation source for the current repository;
- runtime layout;
- trust source or held state; and
- user-hook installation health.

Doctor validates configuration and repairs hook infrastructure, but never writes
the global settings block. It reports malformed patterns, unsafe/symlinked local
settings, missing hooks, and route-marker corruption with actionable guidance.

Policy classification, route selection, activation-marker, and removed
migration-gate failures are fail-closed for Entire work and fail-open for the
user's Git or agent operation: log and skip capture or checkpoint sync without
aborting the host operation. This rule does not weaken existing privacy-critical
behavior in locally activated repositories. In particular, an OPF rewrite or
other established safety gate that currently fails a local pre-push continues
to fail that push.

## Findings disposition

| Finding | Design disposition | Required regression coverage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `01M0TSFS8WSCD7CNSV5XJ4Q983` — migration gate blocks behind prompt/condensation | Remove the takeover migration gate; keep the trust prompt outside route-selection locking | Non-pending pre-push is silent; pending interactive pre-push prompts through `/dev/tty`; concurrent hook and push do not block on route selection |
| `01M0TSFQ9D1EH7M7VCZ43FYVC6` — gate failure aborts commit/push/session | Remove gate; policy/route failures skip Entire work | Separate forced-failure tests prove commit, push, and agent-session host operations succeed; local OPF safety failure still aborts push |
| `01M0TSEWA8GW6BMQEM98Y5AYMS` — committed project settings grant egress | Require machine-local activation or user-global trust; committed settings are not consent | Fresh clone with committed `enabled: true` neither gains local activation nor egress |
| `01M0TSE2YQG4NHX4HQPK7P7FW6` — symlinked `.entire` bypasses executable-setting trust | Reject symlink-traversing local settings and use an explicit hook-time field whitelist | Real clone fixture with tracked `.entire` symlink plus malicious OPF, checkpoint destination, external-agent, hook-path, and strategy values cannot influence hook execution or egress |
| `01M0TSDJQKTMR26TPV0Z1N7YG8` — accessible prompt auto-grants or panics | Preserve the prompt but require an explicit supported selection; otherwise hold | `ACCESSIBLE=1` never grants the default implicitly, never consumes Git stdin, and never panics; explicit selections retain Yes/Not now/Always semantics |
| `01M0TSGCWR0EVVQWK526A4BTEZ` — already-expired try-lock context | Remove try-lock and takeover migration | Barrier-controlled concurrent route-selection test proves both callers return the same complete winner and local enable records activation separately |
| `01M0TSEY7XNH32BR7ZXEGEMABS` — revoke misses stale origin after identity flip | Preserve trust/revoke and record the exact keys written by each CLI/prompt grant so later re-grant/revoke can remove its stale identities without deleting hand-authored entries | Origin→path→origin, path→origin→path, and multiple fetch/push URL cases leave only the intended grant and revoke every recorded identity |
| `01M0TSGEJB4B513AV3TS310RN0` — disable message contradicts `trust_all` | Remove global disable command; require active policy in egress decision | Disabled global tier is inactive even with `trust_all: true` |

Two older GitHub comments are also covered: the preserved prompt derives its
folder-versus-origin label from the same identity used by the gate and writer,
and the hold message remains concise and actionable.

## Testing strategy

### Policy matrix

Table-driven tests cover combinations of:

- user-global absent, disabled, enabled, malformed, or excluded;
- local activation marker absent or present;
- project `enabled` absent, true, or false;
- settings path ordinary, tracked, symlinked, unreadable, or malformed;
- origin absent, normalized, changed, or unparseable; and
- trust absent, global, origin, or path based.

Every case asserts activation source, inactive reason, runtime layout, egress
decision, and trust source from one policy evaluation.

### Runtime and concurrency

- Global-first route remains git-side after ordinary `entire enable`.
- Explicit-first route remains worktree-local after global settings change.
- Simultaneous first global hook and explicit enable converge on one route.
- A synchronization-barrier race between conflicting proposals publishes one
  complete route; both callers reread the same winner, and local activation is
  recorded independently.
- Linked worktrees receive distinct markers and runtime roots.
- Enabling a main worktree does not locally activate a newly added sibling that
  contains committed `enabled: true` settings.
- Legacy bootstrap accepts only the enumerated per-worktree record/file shapes;
  an external `core.hooksPath` is insufficient even in a single-worktree repo.
- Enable-after-uninstall selects the worktree route with global policy off and
  the git-common route with global policy on, replacing the disabled tombstone
  in both cases.
- Route-resolution failure skips capture without failing the host operation.
- No runtime migration, transcript rewrite, or long-held flock is exercised
  because those components no longer exist.

### Hooks and security

- User hooks are installed idempotently regardless of global opt-in.
- Disabled global policy reaches the cheapest fail-closed path.
- Agent hook specifications drive install, recognition, removal, and count.
- Claude Code and all twelve current Gemini entries remain present with the same
  command forms, matchers, deduplication, and event behavior.
- Committed and symlinked repository settings cannot activate executable
  behavior or egress in a fresh clone.
- Every executable/outbound field in the provenance matrix is pinned by a
  malicious committed-value test.
- Multiple fetch and push URLs all require explicit trust; an unparseable or
  untrusted secondary URL holds egress.
- Accessible mode cannot grant consent implicitly or consume pre-push stdin;
  explicit Yes/Not now/Always choices retain their current effects.
- A repository-wide user-facing-string check finds no remaining instructions to
  run `entire enable --global` or `entire disable --global`; activation guidance
  points to the resolved user settings file instead.
- `status`, `help`, `version`, `auth token`, and JSON inspection commands create
  no route, activation, settings, or agent-hook files.

### Integration

Real-binary integration tests cover:

1. settings-file enable -> agent hook activity -> hidden capture;
2. untrusted pending checkpoint -> interactive Yes/Not now/Always behavior,
   plus non-interactive successful branch push with held checkpoints;
3. `entire trust`, pre-push trust, and settings-file origin/path trust -> queued
   checkpoint drain;
4. explicit enable after global capture -> same runtime route and continuous
   session visibility;
5. fresh clone with committed settings -> no local activation or executable
   behavior; and
6. linked-worktree isolation.

Run focused tests during development and `mise run check` before every commit.
Run deterministic canaries as part of the repository check. Real-agent E2E tests
remain opt-in and require explicit user authorization.

## Landing strategy

The refactor is prepared from `main` as one coherent review unit, not as another
layer on the old stack. The implementation should be organized into logical
commits:

1. policy and provenance model;
2. sticky runtime-route marker and removal of takeover migration;
3. settings-only global surface and egress behavior;
4. declarative, automatically reconciled user hooks;
5. status/doctor/documentation updates; and
6. integration coverage and removal of obsolete tests/helpers.

PR #2030 may retain its public review location, but its head should present the
coherent final implementation rather than the current stacked merge history.
Before any remote update, lint and the full repository check must pass. After a
push, all repository and PR gates must reach terminal status; risk/security
metrics are compared and every valid finding is addressed before completion.

Trail findings are resolved only after the corresponding implementation and
regression test are present on the trail branch.

## Alternatives considered

### Delete commands but retain takeover migration

This is the smallest textual change, but it preserves repeated policy reads,
long-lived hook locks, route-transition races, and most of the current test
surface. It does not address the architectural cause of the findings.

### Move every repository to git-side runtime storage

A universal git-common-dir runtime is the cleanest abstract model, but it would
force a migration on every existing explicitly enabled repository and change
established `.entire/logs`, `metadata`, and `tmp` behavior. That expansion is not
required to make the unmerged global feature coherent.

### Remove interactive trust while making activation settings-only

This would simplify pre-push, but it would regress an intentional consent flow
and force users to leave their push to configure egress. The chosen design keeps
the prompt, isolates it from route-selection locks and Git stdin, and fixes the
accessible-mode behavior without removing the feature.

### Infer local activation from committed project settings

This preserves the current short circuit but lets cloned content grant egress
and unlock executable configuration. Machine-local activation evidence is the
necessary security boundary once user-level hooks are installed everywhere.

content.content:
# Settings-Only Global Tracking Refactor Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Replace the stacked global-enable implementation with one coherent policy-and-routing architecture while preserving pre-push trust, checkpoint egress, and the complete Claude Code and Gemini CLI hook behavior.

**Architecture:** A leaf package under `cmd/entire/cli/settings/repopolicy` owns user-global settings, repository policy classification, machine-local activation, immutable runtime routing, and trust identity. Existing `settings` APIs become compatibility facades while consumers migrate to one immutable `RepoPolicy` snapshot. Runtime routing is sticky per worktree, lazy setup is component-versioned, and the old enable/wizard/takeover migration paths are deleted.

**Tech Stack:** Go 1.26, Cobra, Charm `huh`, go-git v6, repository `flock` and `jsonutil` helpers, table-driven Go tests, integration-tag tests, Vogon deterministic E2E canary.

---

## Scope and execution notes

- Work in the existing dedicated `global-settings-tier` worktree.
- Preserve `bca00205a` and branch `fix/global-takeover-migration` as the stacked reference while refactoring.
- The design and this plan are local artifacts under ignored `docs/superpowers`; do not add or commit them.
- Do not run real-agent E2E tests. `mise run check` runs only the approved deterministic canaries.
- Before writing Go in each task, search for reusable helpers with `rg` because the documented `/go:discover-related` skill is not installed in this environment.
- Every top-level test and subtest uses `t.Parallel()` unless it calls `t.Chdir`, `t.Setenv`, or modifies another process-global seam.
- Every Git-touching test uses `testutil.InitRepo`, repository-local identity/GPG config, and a temp worktree.
- Before every commit run `mise run check`. Before any push rerun `mise run lint` after the final formatter pass.
- Recorded intent from Entire checkpoints and commit history that must survive:
  - the disabled/unconfigured global fast path performs no Git subprocess;
  - invalid exclusions fail closed;
  - global-only tracking never writes `.entire/metadata`, `logs`, or `tmp` into the worktree;
  - lazy setup never turns an agent/Git hook failure into a failed host operation;
  - pre-push consent remains Yes / Not now / Always and Git stdin is never used;
  - Claude/Gemini user-hook installs preserve unrelated configuration and deduplicate against repo-scope production hooks.

## Final file structure

### New leaf policy package

- `cmd/entire/cli/settings/repopolicy/types.go`: immutable policy, activation, route, trust, and reason types.
- `cmd/entire/cli/settings/repopolicy/user_settings.go`: strict user settings schema, loading, validation, locking, and atomic writes.
- `cmd/entire/cli/settings/repopolicy/repository.go`: Git/worktree facts and stable worktree namespace resolution without importing `paths` or parent `settings`.
- `cmd/entire/cli/settings/repopolicy/activation.go`: project-settings provenance, activation marker, legacy bootstrap, and disable tombstone.
- `cmd/entire/cli/settings/repopolicy/route.go`: route registry, atomic first-writer-wins selection, and policy context memo.
- `cmd/entire/cli/settings/repopolicy/policy.go`: read-only `ClassifyRepoPolicy` and mutating `EnsureRuntimeRoute` orchestration.
- `cmd/entire/cli/settings/repopolicy/trust.go`: trust identity, egress decision, trust writers, and grant ledger.
- Matching focused `_test.go` files beside each responsibility.

### Existing packages

- `cmd/entire/cli/settings/global.go`: shrink to aliases/facades plus public diagnostics helpers; no independent policy tree.
- `cmd/entire/cli/settings/hook_settings.go`: convert verified provenance into a positive-whitelist `EntireSettings` view for hook-time consumers.
- `cmd/entire/cli/settings/trust.go`: shrink to compatibility facades or delete once callers use `repopolicy`.
- `cmd/entire/cli/paths/invisible.go`: construct runtime paths from a resolved route; delete settings parsing and activation mirrors.
- `cmd/entire/cli/setup_global.go`: retain user-hook reconciliation helpers only; delete global activation commands, wizard, and runtime migration.

{"body":"## Summary

As a less-technical user (Product Manager) who uses Claude Code for rapid prototyping, I frequently spin up quick POCs — creating new repos, committing code, and moving on. I don't follow a traditional developer workflow where I `cd` into a project directory, set up tooling, and then start working. I often create repos on the fly via `gh repo create` or let Claude Code scaffold things directly.

**The problem:** Entire currently requires per-repo configuration (`entire configure` or `entire enable`) before it can track agent sessions. This means any work done in an unconfigured repo is invisible to Entire. For users who move fast and create repos frequently, this is a significant gap — the most interesting agent sessions (the messy, exploratory POC work) are exactly the ones that never get tracked.

## Proposed Behavior

A global configuration mode that automatically enables Entire tracking for **any** git repo where an agent session starts, without requiring per-repo setup first.

Possible implementations:
- **Global agent hooks** installed at the user level (e.g., via `git config --global core.hooksPath` or a Claude Code user-level hook) that detect agent activity and auto-initialize Entire tracking
- **`entire enable --global`** flag that sets a user-level default: "track all repos unless explicitly disabled"
- **Git template directory integration** (`init.templateDir`) so every new `git init` or `git clone` automatically gets Entire hooks
- **Agent-side integration** — Claude Code (and other agents) could check for Entire and auto-configure on session start if global mode is enabled

## Why This Matters

The current per-repo model works well for developers who have a stable set of projects. But for users who:
- Use AI agents as thinking/prototyping tools (not just coding tools)
- Create throwaway repos for POCs, demos, or explorations
- Work across many repos in a single day
- Don't have `entire configure` as part of their muscle memory

...the friction of per-repo setup means Entire misses the very sessions that would benefit most from being tracked. The "commit log for agents" value proposition is strongest when it's **always on**, like how shell history works — you don't configure it per-directory.

## Context

This came up while testing Entire CLI on a new project created during a Claude Code session. The agent created the repo, built the code, committed, and pushed — but because the session was initiated from a different directory, Entire captured zero checkpoints. The work was done, but the "why" behind it was lost.

Related: #985 (global export/viewing across repos) addresses the *read* side of this problem. This issue addresses the *write* side — making sure sessions are captured in the first place.

## Environment
- Entire CLI v0.5.x
- Claude Code (claude-opus-4-6)
- macOS","nComments":3,"title":"[Feature Request] Global auto-enable: track agent sessions without per-repo configuration"}

[User] well yeah activate immediately, and isn't that hte point of global enable
[Assistant] Exactly. Global enable must start tracking immediately; migration is cleanup, not a prerequisite. The case here is later promoting one globally tracked repo to explicit repo-level enable, and that promotion should also take effect immediately.
[Assistant] Yes—that is the contract: tracking activates immediately; migration must never delay or block it.
I considered three approaches:
1. **Flip routing first, migrate opportunistically — recommended.**
   Write repo activation first, clear the routing cache, then attempt a non-blocking migration. New hooks immediately use `.entire/`; an already-running hook may finish in the old namespace, so migration defers safely.
2. Hold a lock across activation and migration.
   Strongly atomic, but `entire enable` could wait on active hooks, conflicting with immediate activation.
3. Temporarily dual-read/write both namespaces.
   More tolerant, but significantly more complexity and long-term cleanup behavior.
Proposed design:
- Implement in **layer C, trail 1014 / PR #1955**, where enable-time migration lives.
- Change all first-activation paths to persist repo settings before migration.
- Make migration-gate acquisition non-blocking; a busy gate or active session prints the existing deferred-migration notice and returns success.
- Keep old routed data intact until migration can run safely.
- During successful migration, rewrite idle session `TranscriptPath` values from the old routed prefix to the new `.entire/` prefix.
- On later `entire enable`, also repair previously migrated stale paths even if no old files remain.
- Add regression tests for:
  - activation returning while an active hook/session exists;
  - every subsequent hook routing to `.entire/`;
  - pre-flip hook data remaining recoverable;
  - idle OpenCode/Pi transcript paths being repaired;
  - existing repo-level behavior remaining unchanged.
- Merge the fixing commit forward into layers D and E.
`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
Writing the routing discriminator first is the key simplification. Once repo settings exist, every newly started process chooses the worktree route; migration can then be safely treated as retryable garbage collection rather than part of activation.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
Approve this design and I’ll write the short spec, review it, and move directly into the implementation plan.
[User] what is the migration excatly?
[Assistant] The migration is only a **local storage-location move inside the same repository**. It is not session adoption or cross-repo movement.
Under global enable, Entire keeps runtime files invisibly under the Git common directory:
```text
.git/entire/worktree/<worktree-hash>/
├── metadata/   # session state, prompts, checkpoint bookkeeping
├── logs/
└── tmp/        # cached agent transcripts, including OpenCode/Pi
```
If the user later runs ordinary `entire enable` in that repo, it becomes explicitly repo-enabled. Runtime data should then live in the normal location:
```text
.entire/
├── metadata/
├── logs/
└── tmp/
```
The migration moves the current worktree’s files from the first location to the second, without overwriting conflicting destination files. It leaves sibling worktrees untouched.
It does **not** move:
- settings or `.gitignore`;
- Git hooks or checkpoint refs;
- data between repositories;
- another worktree’s sessions.
The bug is that a moved session-state file can still contain an absolute `TranscriptPath` pointing to the old `.git/.../tmp/...` location. The fix repairs that pointer to `.entire/tmp/...`.
`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
Global tracking remains active throughout. This migration happens only when a globally tracked repo is later promoted to explicit repo-level enable; it converts invisible runtime storage into the repo’s standard runtime layout.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
[User] how about agent config files?
[Assistant] I’m checking the actual agent-install paths because these are separate from `.entire` runtime data: global enable uses user-level agent hooks where supported, while ordinary repo enable may write repo-scoped agent configuration.
[Assistant] Agent configuration files are separate and should **not** be migrated.
With global enable:
- Entire writes user-level hooks only for currently supported agents:
  - `~/.claude/settings.json`
  - `~/.gemini/settings.json`
- It creates no repo-level agent configuration.
If that repository is later explicitly enabled:
- Normal `entire enable` may install repo-level agent configuration such as `.claude/settings.json` or `.gemini/settings.json`.
- The user-level hooks remain because they still provide global tracking for every other repository.
- Claude and Gemini deduplicate identical user-level and repo-level Entire hook commands, so they should fire once.
- Other agents receive repo-level configuration only; they currently lack verified global-hook support.
Therefore the migration handles only:
```text
metadata/
logs/
tmp/
```
It does not copy, move, or remove either user-level or repo-level agent configs.
`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The `.entire` migration changes where session runtime state lives. Agent configs are activation surfaces: user-level configs awaken Entire globally, while repo-level configs opt one repository into that agent explicitly. Keeping those concerns separate avoids breaking global coverage.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
[User] but the lazy install handles the metadata/
  logs/
  tmp/ and githooks on all repos?
[Assistant] Yes, with two important distinctions:
1. `entire enable --global` does **not scan every repository immediately**.
2. `metadata/`, `logs/`, and `tmp/` are **created on demand**, not preinstalled.
For each eligible repo, the first supported agent hook—currently Claude Code or Gemini—triggers lazy setup:
- Checks global settings and exclusions.
- Installs Entire’s Git hooks into the Git directory.
- Creates/repairs the checkpoint metadata ref.
- Records the clone-level lazy-setup marker.
- Routes runtime files invisibly to:
```text
<git-common-dir>/entire/worktree/<worktree-hash>/
├── metadata/
├── logs/
└── tmp/
```
Those directories appear only as normal hook activity needs them. Nothing is created in the worktree, so `git status` remains clean.
Caveats:
- A repo excluded globally or explicitly configured at repo level follows its own behavior.
- If `core.hooksPath` points inside the worktree, lazy setup refuses to install Git hooks because that would violate invisible tracking. Agent-session capture still works, but commit-hook functionality requires explicit repo enable.
- Agents without verified user-level hooks cannot initiate global tracking yet; ordinary repo enable is still required for them.
So yes: **every eligible repository touched through a supported globally installed agent hook receives invisible runtime routing and lazy Git-hook setup automatically.**
[User] why not worktree? is that fine, because we just need in repo
[Assistant] Yes, it is still “in the repo”—specifically in the clone’s Git administration directory rather than its checked-out files.
| Data | Global-enable location | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Git hooks | `.git/hooks/` | Repo-local and invisible to Git status |
| Runtime data | `.git/entire/worktree/<hash>/` | Repo-local, invisible, isolated per worktree |
| Agent activation hooks | User config | Must fire before a repo has any Entire setup |
| Checkpoints | Git refs | Durable and syncable |
Putting runtime files directly in the worktree would require creating `.entire/` and probably modifying `.gitignore`. That could:
- Dirty `git status`.
- Conflict with files the repository already owns.
- Accidentally get committed.
- Break the promise that global tracking leaves no footprint in checked-out files.
The `<worktree-hash>` still keeps linked worktrees separate even though they share one Git common directory.
When users explicitly run ordinary `entire enable`, they have opted into repo-visible configuration, so runtime data can move to `<worktree>/.entire/`.
For a worktree-resident `core.hooksPath`, Entire skips lazy Git-hook installation because modifying something like `.husky/` would change checked-out repository files. The user-level agent hook still captures the session; explicit repo enable is required for commit hooks in that unusual configuration.
[User] so it still tracks in worktree?
[Assistant] Yes—**it tracks the session and edits in that worktree**, but stores the runtime files outside the checked-out file tree.
For example:
```text
Worktree being tracked:
/repo-feature/
Invisible storage:
<git-common-dir>/entire/worktree/<hash-of-repo-feature>/
```
The session state records the worktree path, file changes are detected relative to that worktree, and checkpoints belong to that repository. The hash keeps multiple linked worktrees isolated.
So:
- **Logical ownership:** the worktree.
- **Physical storage:** the repository’s Git directory.
- **Visible worktree footprint:** none.

## What actually happened to this branch

**The numbers.** Your local `main` is stale (Aug 24), which is where the "13k" comes from. Against `origin/main`, PR #2030 is **+9,989 / −1,037 across 107 files** — ~6.9k production, ~3.1k tests. The five original layers summed to ~12k (+2020, +2699, +3079, +4119), so consolidating them didn't shrink anything by itself; the refactor then added a 3.5k-line `repopolicy` package while keeping the old `settings/global.go`, `settings/trust.go`, `paths/invisible.go` as "compatibility facades" instead of deleting them.

**Why risk/security keep going *up*.** Every automated review finding was treated as a hard acceptance criterion and answered with a *new mechanism*, and each mechanism is itself reviewable surface:

- "Committed `.entire/settings.json` shouldn't count as consent" → a machine-local **`activation.json` marker** → which broke existing enabled repos → **legacy bootstrap** that scans `.entire/metadata/*` files and session records as "evidence" (250 lines) → which breaks when a repo directory moves → **`RebindMovedRepository`** that cross-verifies four registry records (150 lines) → which mis-handles case-only renames on macOS → the newest low finding. That entire chain exists to answer one finding.
- Same pattern for `route.json` (sticky layout + atomic first-writer-wins), `setup.json` (versioned components), a **trust-grant ledger**, **settings provenance** (symlink lstat walk + `git ls-files` subprocesses inside hooks, 296 lines), and a **hook-time field whitelist** (289 lines).
- The root cause upstream of all of it: "settings-only activation, no command" was implemented as **"install user-level Claude/Gemini hooks for *every* Entire user, whether or not they opted into global."** Once hooks fire in every repo on the machine, "did *this user* enable *this repo*?" becomes a security question, and all the machinery above is the answer.

The two open **high** findings right now (`opencode/lifecycle.go:187` and `:213` — OpenCode hard-fails the turn on `IsUnroutableRuntimePath` instead of skipping) are real but small, and the commit `c18bfa1` claims to fix them; the trail just hasn't re-evaluated. They're symptoms, not the problem.

## What the feature minimally needs

Holding your stated constraints fixed (settings-file-only activation; keep pre-push Yes / Not now / Always + `entire trust`; keep Claude Code + Gemini hook coverage; byte-clean worktree in global mode), the design collapses to **one new machine-local record — the user settings file — and derived rules**:

| Concern | Current PR | Proposed |
|---|---|---|
| Activation | `activation.json` + legacy bootstrap + rebind + `enabled` veto via provenance | Repo has `.entire/settings*.json` → **exactly today's behavior**. Else `global.enabled` && not excluded → global mode. `enabled:false` veto falls out for free. |
| Runtime layout | `route.json`, sticky, atomic publish | Derived: local → `.entire/`, global → `<git-common>/entire/worktree/<hash>/`. No marker. |
| Hook-time settings | provenance + whitelist view | Not needed: a global-mode repo *has no repo settings file by definition*; if it does, it's local mode = today's loader (incl. today's OPF local-file rule). |
| User-level hooks | Always installed for everyone | Installed **iff `global.enabled`**, reconciled cheaply on any foreground `entire` command (that's how a settings edit "takes effect" without a command). Global-off users: zero change. |
| Lazy setup | `setup.json` versioned components | Install git hooks (skip when `core.hooksPath` is in-worktree) + ensure ref; `IsGitHookInstalled` is already a cheap file check. |
| Egress | trust gate + ledger | Same gate, no ledger: when global is on, egress needs `trust_all` / trusted origin / trusted path. **`entire enable` records trust automatically** (the user ran it there). Revoke removes the repo's *current* origin keys + path. |
| Status/doctor | ~450 lines | Same facts, ~150 lines. |

Rough size: **~2–2.5k production + ~1.5k tests ≈ 3.5–4k**, versus 9,989. Security posture improves by *removal*: no git subprocesses for provenance inside hooks, no spoofable registries, no relocation heuristics, no evidence scanning, and hooks only on machines that opted in.

**Behavior differences to be honest about:**
1. Committed `enabled:true` activates a clone — that's today's shipped contract (teams commit it). The finding's actual *harm* (egress) stays closed by the trust gate.
2. Users who already have repo-enabled repos and then turn global on get **one** trust prompt per repo on next push ("Always" ends it).
3. A globally-tracked repo later `entire enable`d leaves its old runtime dir under `.git/` (harmless — session state lives in `.git/entire-sessions`, and `full.jsonl` is regenerated each Stop; I'd verify `checkpoint.json`/`content_hash.txt` loss only costs a dedup, not data). No migration, no locks.
4. Revoke after an origin *change* (A→B) doesn't auto-remove A. Document it.

One thing worth pulling out as its own tiny PR against `main` regardless: finding `01M0TSE2YQG4…` (symlinked `.entire/` bypassing the OPF `command` tracked-file check) is a **pre-existing** bug in `settings/opf_command_trust.go`, not a global-mode bug. ~15 lines to lstat the path components.

## How I'd execute

Start a fresh branch from `origin/main` and rebuild the minimal design, lifting the pieces of this branch that are already right (user-settings matching, `hooks_user.go` for both agents, `trust_prompt.go`, `trust_cmd.go`, the `manual_commit_push.go` gate, the unroutable-path skip pattern, status/doctor lines). A subtractive refactor of this branch is the other option, but 174 commits of stack-merge history with facades is what produced the residue in the first place — I'd rather present the reviewer a clean ~4k diff.

**Kept as-is (user-facing):**

- **Pre-push trust prompt** — Yes / Not now / Always, via `/dev/tty`, never Git stdin, never blocks the user's own push; non-interactive pushes hold with the one-line stderr hint.
- **Egress gate** — held checkpoints stay local until trusted; first trusted push drains the backlog; both storage backends.
- `entire trust` / `entire trust --revoke`, `trust_all` / `trusted_origins` / `trusted_paths` in the same settings file.
- Byte-clean worktree in global mode (runtime data under `.git/…`).
- **Warnings/notices**: the session-start "capturing locally via global mode, run `entire trust`" banner, the excluded-repo session-start notice, the pre-push hold message, the one-time global-tracking warning, `status`/`doctor` global + trust lines.

**What changes underneath (and two things you'd notice):**
1. User-level hooks get installed **when `global.enabled` is true**, not for every Entire user. Since there's no command, this happens on the next foreground `entire` command you run after editing the file (e.g. `entire status`, which will also tell you it did it). Doctor repairs them.
2. If you already had repo-enabled repos and then turn global on, you'll see the trust prompt **once** per repo on the next push (or pick "Always"). `entire enable` going forward records trust automatically.

content.text:
Yes — lazy setup stays; it's the core of the feature. The flow when you (via Claude Code or Gemini) touch a repo that has never seen Entire:

1. Your **user-level** Claude/Gemini hook fires → `entire hooks claude-code session-start` runs in that repo.
2. The hook reads `~/.config/entire/settings.json` → global on, repo not excluded, no repo-level `.entire/settings.json` → **global mode**.
3. On that first hook it lazily does the per-repo setup, all inside `.git/`:
   - installs the Entire git hooks into the repo's hooks dir (skipped if `core.hooksPath` points inside the worktree, e.g. `.husky/`, so nothing checked-out is touched);
   - ensures the checkpoint metadata ref;
   - routes `metadata/`, `logs/`, `tmp/` to `<git-common>/entire/worktree/<hash>/` — nothing in the worktree, `git status` stays clean.
4. Session tracks normally; commits get trailers via the lazily installed git hooks; pre-push hits the trust gate.

Two limits, same as the current PR: it only triggers for agents with user-level hook support (Claude Code, Gemini) — a purely human `git commit` in a repo no agent has touched yet doesn't install anything, since there's no hook to fire; and other agents still need repo-level `entire enable`.

What I'm simplifying is only *how it remembers setup was done*: instead of the versioned `setup.json` component record, it re-checks cheaply (is the hook file present, does the ref exist — both are file reads) on each hook. Same behavior, no registry.

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context for our codebase and questionable taste. Document everything they need to know: which files to touch for each task, code, testing, docs they might need to check, how to test it. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

Assume they are a skilled developer, but know almost nothing about our toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** This should be run in a dedicated worktree (created by brainstorming skill).

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Bite-Sized Task Granularity

**Each step is one action (2-5 minutes):**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (if subagents available) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

```python
def test_specific_behavior():
    result = function(input)
    assert result == expected
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"

- [ ] **Step 3: Write minimal implementation**

```python
def function(input):
    return expected
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: PASS

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
```
````

## Remember
- Exact file paths always
- Complete code in plan (not "add validation")
- Exact commands with expected output
- Reference relevant skills with @ syntax
- DRY, YAGNI, TDD, frequent commits

## Plan Review Loop

After completing each chunk of the plan:

1. Dispatch plan-document-reviewer subagent (see plan-document-reviewer-prompt.md) with precisely crafted review context — never your session history. This keeps the reviewer focused on the plan, not your thought process.
   - Provide: chunk content, path to spec document
2. If ❌ Issues Found:
   - Fix the issues in the chunk
   - Re-dispatch reviewer for that chunk
   - Repeat until ✅ Approved
3. If ✅ Approved: proceed to next chunk (or execution handoff if last chunk)

**Chunk boundaries:** Use `## Chunk N: <name>` headings to delimit chunks. Each chunk should be ≤1000 lines and logically self-contained.

**Review loop guidance:**
- Same agent that wrote the plan fixes it (preserves context)
- If loop exceeds 5 iterations, surface to human for guidance
- Reviewers are advisory - explain disagreements if you believe feedback is incorrect

## Execution Handoff

After saving the plan:

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Ready to execute?"**

**Execution path depends on harness capabilities:**

**If harness has subagents (Claude Code, etc.):**
- **REQUIRED:** Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development
- Do NOT offer a choice - subagent-driven is the standard approach
- Fresh subagent per task + two-stage review

**If harness does NOT have subagents:**
- Execute plan in current session using superpowers:executing-plans
- Batch execution with checkpoints for review

+//     cannot be normalized to host/owner/repo — informational: the tier

+	if len(missing) > 0 {
+		fmt.Fprintln(w, "Global tracking: USER-LEVEL AGENT HOOKS MISSING")

+	if problems := settings.ValidateGlobalPatterns(us.Global); len(problems) > 0 {

+		fmt.Fprintln(w, "  Exclude entries fail closed: each deactivates global tracking in every repo it is checked against.")
+		fmt.Fprintln(w, "  trusted_paths entries are skipped: an unusable one never grants checkpoint sync.")
+		for _, p := range problems {

+		fmt.Fprintln(w, "  exclude_origins is configured, but this repo's origin cannot be normalized to host/owner/repo:")

+		}

+	}

+	// Untrusted enrolled repo: informational, never a failure — the hold is
+	// the intended state until the user opts in.

+		default:

+		}
+		fmt.Fprintln(w, "  This is intended until you opt in; run `entire trust` to sync.")
+	}

+			// error as "skip hook installation", so falling into the drift
+			// branch would clear the marker and promise a reinstall that never

+			fmt.Fprintln(w, "Globally tracked clone: GIT HOOK STATE UNVERIFIED")

+			fmt.Fprintln(w, "  Git hooks appear missing but the cause could not be determined; nothing was changed.")
+			return
+		}
+		if resident {
+			fmt.Fprintln(w, "Globally tracked clone: GIT HOOKS SKIPPED (core.hooksPath inside the worktree)")
+			fmt.Fprintf(w, "  core.hooksPath resolves to %s, inside this worktree; global tracking never\n", hooksDir)
+			fmt.Fprintln(w, "  writes worktree files, so its git hooks were deliberately not installed.")
+			fmt.Fprintln(w, "  Agent-side session capture still works; commit-time checkpoint trailers do not.")
+			fmt.Fprintln(w, "  For hook capture, enable Entire in this repo: 'entire enable' (repo-level setup")
+			fmt.Fprintln(w, "  chains into an existing hooks dir), or point core.hooksPath back at .git/hooks.")
+			return
+		}
+		fmt.Fprintln(w, "Globally tracked clone: GIT HOOKS MISSING")
+		fmt.Fprintln(w, "  This clone was enabled by global tracking but its git hooks are gone.")
+		record.GitHooksSpec = 0
+		if clearErr := repopolicy.WriteSetupRecord(repository, record); clearErr != nil {
+			fmt.Fprintf(w, "  Could not mark the git-hook setup component stale (%v).\n", clearErr)
+			fmt.Fprintln(w, "  Run `entire enable` here to restore tracking.")
+			return
+		}

+	}
+}

+		Configured:   true,

# Plan Document Reviewer Prompt Template

Use this template when dispatching a plan document reviewer subagent.

**Purpose:** Verify the plan chunk is complete, matches the spec, and has proper task decomposition.

**Dispatch after:** Each plan chunk is written

```
Task tool (general-purpose):
  description: "Review plan chunk N"
  prompt: |
    You are a plan document reviewer. Verify this plan chunk is complete and ready for implementation.

    **Plan chunk to review:** [PLAN_FILE_PATH] - Chunk N only
    **Spec for reference:** [SPEC_FILE_PATH]

    ## What to Check

    | Category | What to Look For |
    |----------|------------------|
    | Completeness | TODOs, placeholders, incomplete tasks, missing steps |
    | Spec Alignment | Chunk covers relevant spec requirements, no scope creep |
    | Task Decomposition | Tasks atomic, clear boundaries, steps actionable |
    | File Structure | Files have clear single responsibilities, split by responsibility not layer |
    | File Size | Would any new or modified file likely grow large enough to be hard to reason about as a whole? |
    | Task Syntax | Checkbox syntax (`- [ ]`) on steps for tracking |
    | Chunk Size | Each chunk under 1000 lines |

    ## CRITICAL

    Look especially hard for:
    - Any TODO markers or placeholder text
    - Steps that say "similar to X" without actual content
    - Incomplete task definitions
    - Missing verification steps or expected outputs
    - Files planned to hold multiple responsibilities or likely to grow unwieldy

    ## Output Format

    ## Plan Review - Chunk N

    **Status:** Approved | Issues Found

    **Issues (if any):**
    - [Task X, Step Y]: [specific issue] - [why it matters]

    **Recommendations (advisory):**
    - [suggestions that don't block approval]
```

**Reviewer returns:** Status, Issues (if any), Recommendations

Both egress entry points are gated — `ManualCommitStrategy.prePush` (early return beside the single-remote gate, above both backend branches, so held repos never run OPF) and `PushQueuedCheckpointRefs`. A hold never blocks the user's own push: the branch pushes, checkpoint data stays local (refs-backend refs stay queued) with one stderr explanation, and the first trusted push drains the backlog.* — the old sentence "Settings files created for unrelated features do not grant egress." is **dropped**: under `ReadRepoActivation` a project `settings.json` without an `enabled` key is default-enabled, exactly as on main. lines: +5. Align `IsSetUpAndEnabled` with the new predicate so the two gates cannot disagree:
+// IsSetUpAndEnabled reports repo-level activation: a project settings.json
+// (default enabled) or a settings.local.json carrying an explicit "enabled"
+// key, with the local value winning. Any read error is disabled (fail closed).

+Delete `repoSettingsEnabled` if it is then unreferenced. **Accepted deviation from main, state it in the commit body:** main's `IsSetUpAndEnabled` was `IsSetUpAny && Load().Enabled`, so a repo whose *only* settings file is a hand-written `settings.local.json` without an `enabled` key (e.g. `{"log_level":"DEBUG"}`) counted as set up. Under `ReadRepoActivation` it does not, so with the global tier off such a repo is inactive. `entire enable --local` always writes the key (`Enabled bool` has no `omitempty`), so this only affects hand-authored files; the benefit is that a local file written by an unrelated feature (investigate config) no longer pins a globally tracked repo into local mode.
`settings/checkpoints.go`: delete the `RepoPolicyFromContext` special case and the `repopolicy` import.

+Rationale for the deletion (put a version of this in the commit body): a repo the global tier activates has, by definition, no project `settings.json` and no local file with an `enabled` key. It may still carry an untracked `settings.local.json` for other keys; `Load` merges that developer-owned file exactly as on main, with the existing tracked-layer rejection and `enforceOPFCommandTrust` still applying — so no separate sanitized view is needed.

input.old_string: In `integration_test/global_enable_test.go`: `TestGlobalEnable_LazyInvisibleSetup` asserts hooks installed, `refs/entire/...` primary ref exists, `git status --porcelain` empty, no `.entire` in the worktree, runtime data under `.git/entire/worktree/<hash>/` — replace its `ReadSetupRecord` block with `strategy.IsGitHookInstalledInDir` + an `os.Stat` of `<runtimeRoot>/primary-ref-ready` (compute the root via `repopolicy.ClassifyRepoPolicyAt(ctx, env.RepoDir)`). `TestGlobalEnable_GitHookRouteTriggersSetup` today deletes `setup.json` to force a re-run; there is no record any more, and deleting the git hooks would leave nothing to fire. Reshape it into two tests: (a) `TestGlobalEnable_GitHookRouteRepairsPrimaryRef` — after the first session, delete the `primary-ref-ready` stamp **and** the primary ref (`git update-ref -d <ref>`; use the same ref name the existing test reads), commit through `env.GitCommitWithShadowHooksAsAgent`, assert the ref and the stamp are back; (b) `TestGlobalEnable_AgentRouteReinstallsGitHooks` — `os.RemoveAll(<git-dir>/hooks)`, fire `user-prompt-submit` via `runClaudeHook`, assert `strategy.IsGitHookInstalledInDir(ctx, env.RepoDir)`. `TestGlobalEnable_TierAbsent_CreatesNothing` stays.
input.new_string: In `integration_test/global_enable_test.go`: **never classify in-process here** — these tests are `t.Parallel()` and the per-test `{"global":{"enabled":true}}` config dir reaches only the spawned binary via `extraEnv`; the test process sees TestMain's shared `ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR`, so `ClassifyRepoPolicyAt` would report inactive and `RuntimeRoot()` would point at `<repo>/.entire`. Compute the git-side root with pure path math: `repository, _ := repopolicy.ResolveRepositoryAt(ctx, env.RepoDir); runtimeRoot := repopolicy.RuntimeDir(repository)` (or reuse the file's existing `invisibleBase` = `.git/entire/worktree/<paths.HashWorktreeID("")>`). `TestGlobalEnable_LazyInvisibleSetup` asserts hooks installed, `entire/checkpoints/v1` exists, `git status --porcelain` empty, no `.entire` in the worktree, runtime data under that root — replace its `ReadSetupRecord` block with `strategy.IsGitHookInstalledInDir` + `os.Stat(filepath.Join(runtimeRoot, "primary-ref-ready"))`. `TestGlobalEnable_GitHookRouteTriggersSetup` today deletes `setup.json` to force a re-run; there is no record any more, and deleting the git hooks would leave nothing to fire. Reshape it into two tests: (a) `TestGlobalEnable_GitHookRouteRepairsPrimaryRef` — after the first session, `os.Remove` the stamp **and** delete the primary ref with `git update-ref -d refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1` (run via `exec.CommandContext` with `cmd.Dir = env.RepoDir`, `cmd.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()`), commit through `env.GitCommitWithShadowHooksAsAgent` (it execs the real binary's `hooks git prepare-commit-msg`/`post-commit`, whose `PersistentPreRun` calls `MaybeEnsureGlobalSetup`), assert `env.BranchExists("entire/checkpoints/v1")` and the stamp are back; (b) `TestGlobalEnable_AgentRouteReinstallsGitHooks` — `os.RemoveAll(filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".git", "hooks"))`, fire `user-prompt-submit` via `runClaudeHook`, assert `strategy.IsGitHookInstalledInDir(ctx, env.RepoDir)`. `TestGlobalEnable_TierAbsent_CreatesNothing` stays.

input.old_string: Delete the `RepoActivationConfigured` "not applicable — explicitly enabled" branch in `runTrust`. Update `Short` to "Allow this repo's checkpoints to sync while global tracking is on" and `Long`: trust applies to any repo once global tracking is on; `entire enable` records it automatically; this command is for repos that are tracked globally or were enabled before global tracking was turned on. `refuseTrustWhenInactive`'s "global tracking is off" branch stays (an inactive repo has nothing to sync).
input.new_string: Delete the `RepoActivationConfigured` "not applicable — explicitly enabled" branch in `runTrust`. Update `Short` to "Allow this repo's checkpoints to sync while global tracking is on" and `Long`: trust applies to any repo once global tracking is on; `entire enable` records it automatically; this command is for repos that are tracked globally or were enabled before global tracking was turned on. In `refuseTrustWhenInactive`, add a check **before** the activation check: if `us.GlobalConfigured() && !us.GlobalEnabled()`, refuse with the existing "Not recording trust: global tracking is off…" message regardless of repo activation — a repo-enabled repo is `Active` under the derived model even with the tier disabled, and without this guard `entire trust` would write an entry into a disabled tier and print "✓ Trusted" for a repo whose egress is already allowed. The "excluded" and "inactive" branches stay as they are. The second hold message in `PushQueuedCheckpointRefs` (`manual_commit_push.go` ~487, "refs stay queued") has no "global mode" wording and needs no change.

Load plan, review critically, execute all tasks, report when complete.

3. Run verifications as specified
4. Mark as completed

package strategy

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"

	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/session"
	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/settings/repopolicy"
	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/testutil"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

// newGloballyTrackedRepo creates a git repo with no repo-level settings, makes
// it the cwd, and enables the user-global tier for it. Not parallel-safe
// (t.Chdir, t.Setenv).
func newGloballyTrackedRepo(t *testing.T) string {
	t.Helper()
	dir := t.TempDir()
	testutil.InitRepo(t, dir)
	testutil.WriteFile(t, dir, "README.md", "hi\n")
	testutil.GitAdd(t, dir, "README.md")
	testutil.GitCommit(t, dir, "init")
	t.Chdir(dir)
	session.ClearGitCommonDirCache()
	t.Cleanup(session.ClearGitCommonDirCache)
	enrollRepoGlobally(t, `{"global":{"enabled":true}}`)
	return dir
}

func globalRuntimeRootForTest(t *testing.T) string {
	t.Helper()
	policy, err := repopolicy.ClassifyRepoPolicy(t.Context())
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Equal(t, repopolicy.ActivationGlobal, policy.ActivationSource, "fixture must be globally tracked")
	return policy.RuntimeRoot()
}

func TestMaybeEnsureGlobalSetup_InstallsHooksAndRefUnderGit(t *testing.T) {
	dir := newGloballyTrackedRepo(t)
	ctx := t.Context()

	MaybeEnsureGlobalSetup(ctx)

	require.True(t, IsGitHookInstalled(ctx), "git hooks installed by lazy setup")
	stamp := filepath.Join(globalRuntimeRootForTest(t), primaryRefStamp)
	_, err := os.Stat(stamp)
	require.NoError(t, err, "primary-ref stamp written under the git common dir")
	_, err = os.Lstat(filepath.Join(dir, ".entire"))
	require.True(t, os.IsNotExist(err), "global mode must not create a worktree .entire directory")

	// Idempotent: a second call rewrites nothing.
	hookPath := filepath.Join(dir, ".git", "hooks", "post-commit")
	before, err := os.Stat(hookPath)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	MaybeEnsureGlobalSetup(ctx)
	after, err := os.Stat(hookPath)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Equal(t, before.ModTime(), after.ModTime(), "second run must not rewrite installed hooks")
}

func TestMaybeEnsureGlobalSetup_SkipsHooksWhenHooksPathIsInWorktree(t *testing.T) {
	dir := newGloballyTrackedRepo(t)
	ctx := t.Context()
	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "config", "core.hooksPath", ".husky")
	cmd.Dir = dir
	cmd.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()
	out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
	require.NoError(t, err, string(out))

	MaybeEnsureGlobalSetup(ctx)

	_, err = os.Lstat(filepath.Join(dir, ".husky"))
	require.True(t, os.IsNotExist(err), "a worktree-resident hooks dir must never be created")
	_, err = os.Lstat(filepath.Join(dir, ".entire"))
	require.True(t, os.IsNotExist(err), "global mode must not create a worktree .entire directory")
	_, err = os.Stat(filepath.Join(globalRuntimeRootForTest(t), primaryRefStamp))
	require.NoError(t, err, "the ref half of lazy setup still completes")
}

func TestMaybeEnsureGlobalSetup_ProbeErrorWritesNothing(t *testing.T) {
	dir := newGloballyTrackedRepo(t)
	ctx := t.Context()
	SetHooksDirProbeErrorForTesting(errors.New("boom"))
	t.Cleanup(func() { SetHooksDirProbeErrorForTesting(nil) })

	MaybeEnsureGlobalSetup(ctx)

	require.False(t, IsGitHookInstalled(ctx), "no hooks when the hooks dir cannot be resolved")
	_, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(globalRuntimeRootForTest(t), primaryRefStamp))
	require.True(t, os.IsNotExist(err), "no stamp when setup bailed before the ref step")
	_, err = os.Lstat(filepath.Join(dir, ".entire"))
	require.True(t, os.IsNotExist(err))
}

func TestMaybeEnsureGlobalSetup_NoopForRepoEnabledRepo(t *testing.T) {
	dir := newGloballyTrackedRepo(t)
	writeEnabledRepoSettings(t, dir)
	ctx := context.Background()

	MaybeEnsureGlobalSetup(ctx)

	require.False(t, IsGitHookInstalled(ctx), "repo-level activation is not the lazy path's job")
}

	stamp := filepath.Join(globalRuntimeRootForTest(t), primaryRefStamp)

	require.NoError(t, err, "primary-ref stamp written under the git common dir")
	_, err = os.Lstat(filepath.Join(dir, ".entire"))
	require.True(t, os.IsNotExist(err), "global mode must not create a worktree .entire directory")

	hookPath := filepath.Join(dir, ".git", "hooks", "post-commit")
	before, err := os.Stat(hookPath)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	MaybeEnsureGlobalSetup(ctx)
	after, err := os.Stat(hookPath)
	require.NoError(t, err)

}

func TestMaybeEnsureGlobalSetup_SkipsHooksWhenHooksPathIsInWorktree(t *testing.T) {
	dir := newGloballyTrackedRepo(t)
	ctx := t.Context()
	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "config", "core.hooksPath", ".husky")
	cmd.Dir = dir
	cmd.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()
	out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
	require.NoError(t, err, string(out))

	MaybeEnsureGlobalSetup(ctx)

	_, err = os.Lstat(filepath.Join(dir, ".husky"))
	require.True(t, os.IsNotExist(err), "a worktree-resident hooks dir must never be created")
	_, err = os.Lstat(filepath.Join(dir, ".entire"))
	require.True(t, os.IsNotExist(err), "global mode must not create a worktree .entire directory")
	_, err = os.Stat(filepath.Join(globalRuntimeRootForTest(t), primaryRefStamp))
	require.NoError(t, err, "the ref half of lazy setup still completes")
}

func TestMaybeEnsureGlobalSetup_ProbeErrorWritesNothing(t *testing.T) {
	dir := newGloballyTrackedRepo(t)
	ctx := t.Context()
	SetHooksDirProbeErrorForTesting(errors.New("boom"))
	t.Cleanup(func() { SetHooksDirProbeErrorForTesting(nil) })

	MaybeEnsureGlobalSetup(ctx)

	require.False(t, IsGitHookInstalled(ctx), "no hooks when the hooks dir cannot be resolved")
	_, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(globalRuntimeRootForTest(t), primaryRefStamp))
	require.True(t, os.IsNotExist(err), "no stamp when setup bailed before the ref step")
	_, err = os.Lstat(filepath.Join(dir, ".entire"))
	require.True(t, os.IsNotExist(err))
}

func TestMaybeEnsureGlobalSetup_NoopForRepoEnabledRepo(t *testing.T) {
	dir := newGloballyTrackedRepo(t)
	writeEnabledRepoSettings(t, dir)
	ctx := context.Background()

	MaybeEnsureGlobalSetup(ctx)

	require.False(t, IsGitHookInstalled(ctx), "repo-level activation is not the lazy path's job")
}

input.content:
# Global Tracking

Global tracking lets Entire capture agent sessions in every git repository on
a machine without running `entire enable` in each one. It is configured only
in the user's settings file — there is no `enable --global` command and no
wizard — and it is built from two inputs that already exist: the repository's
own `.entire/settings*.json` and the user's `~/.config/entire/settings.json`.
Nothing under `.git/` is a policy record; the only files Entire writes there
in global mode are runtime data and one stamp.

## The settings file

`~/.config/entire/settings.json` (or `$ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR/settings.json`) is
strict-decoded; an unknown key or malformed JSON turns the tier off machine-wide
(fail closed) and `entire doctor` says so.

```json
{
  "global": {
    "enabled": true,
    "exclude_paths": ["~/scratch/**"],
    "exclude_paths_exact": ["~"],
    "exclude_origins": ["github.com/acme/private-*"],
    "trust_all": false,
    "trusted_origins": ["github.com/acme/widgets"],
    "trusted_paths": ["/Users/me/code/notes"]
  }
}
```

- `enabled` — both `true` and `false` count as *configured*; an absent block is
  *unconfigured* (zero cost, no user-level hooks).
- `exclude_paths` — `~`-expanded doublestar globs against the worktree root (a
  bare directory pattern excludes its subtree). `exclude_paths_exact` matches
  one root only, no cascade — the way to exclude `$HOME` as a dotfiles repo
  without excluding everything under it. `exclude_origins` — globs against the
  origin URL normalized to `host/owner/repo`. An unusable pattern, or an origin
  that is present but cannot be normalized, deactivates the tier for that repo
  (fail closed).
- `trust_all`, `trusted_origins`, `trusted_paths` — checkpoint-egress consent
  (below). `entire trust` writes these; users may edit them by hand.

## Activation (derived, never recorded)

`repopolicy.ClassifyRepoPolicy` derives one `RepoPolicy` per process from the
repository's own settings files first and the user file second
(`cmd/entire/cli/settings/repopolicy/policy.go`):

| Repo settings | User `global.enabled` | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| project `settings.json` (default enabled) or `settings.local.json` with an explicit `enabled` key | any | **Local** activation if enabled; an explicit `enabled: false` is a veto that also blocks the tier |
| none | `true`, repo not excluded | **Global** activation |
| none | `false`, absent, or repo excluded | inactive |

This is main's `IsSetUpAndEnabled` contract for repo-enabled repos, with one
deliberate refinement: a `settings.local.json` written by an unrelated feature
(investigate config, …) without an `enabled` key does not pin a globally
tracked repo into local mode. Committed `.entire/settings.json` activates a
fresh clone exactly as it does today — consent for *egress* is a separate
question (below), so cloned content never opens the sync path by itself.

Hooks classify once (`prepareHookPolicy`) and carry the snapshot on `ctx`; a
repo-enabled repo whose settings the full loader rejects (`ErrScannerConfig`)
stays inactive for hooks, as on main. Classification errors fail closed for
Entire's work and never fail the user's git or agent operation.

## Runtime layout (a function of activation source)

`RepoPolicy.RuntimeRoot()` decides where `.entire/{metadata,logs,tmp}` live:

- **Local** → `<worktree>/.entire/…` (main's layout, unchanged).
- **Global** → `<git-common-dir>/entire/worktree/<worktree-hash>/…` — nothing in
  the checked-out tree, so `git status --porcelain` stays byte-clean; linked
  worktrees get separate roots.

`paths.AbsPath` routes only those three prefixes; configuration
(`.entire/settings*.json`) always resolves to the literal worktree. A repo that
was captured globally and is later `entire enable`d switches to the worktree
layout for new activity; its earlier git-side runtime data is left in place
(no migration — `full.jsonl` is regenerated each Stop, and session state lives
in `.git/entire-sessions` regardless). `disable --uninstall` removes it.

## Lazy per-repo setup

The first hook in a globally tracked repo (`strategy.MaybeEnsureGlobalSetup`,
from both the agent-hook and git-hook routes) installs Entire's git hooks and
ensures the checkpoint metadata ref. Git-hook presence is re-checked on every
hook (a file read), so deleted or outdated hooks come back on the next
activity; the ref step is guarded by a `primary-ref-ready` stamp in the
runtime root. When `core.hooksPath` resolves inside the worktree (a committed
`.husky/`), the hooks half is skipped — global tracking never writes into the
checked-out tree; agent-side capture still works and `entire doctor` explains
it. Every failure logs at Debug and returns.

## User-level agent hooks

Claude Code (`~/.claude/settings.json`) and Gemini CLI
(`~/.gemini/settings.json`) support user-level hooks with the same inventory
and command form as the repo-level ones, so each agent deduplicates them.
`globalPostRun` (root `PersistentPostRun`, plus the installer) reconciles them
against the tier on every foreground `entire` command: installed while
`global.enabled` is true for agents present on the machine, removed when the
tier is configured but off, untouched while unconfigured. That is how a hand
edit of the settings file takes effect without a dedicated command. Hook
processes are hidden commands and never reconcile.

## Checkpoint egress and trust

`settings.CheckpointEgressAllowed` (`repopolicy.DecideEgress`) is the single
predicate for whether checkpoint data may leave the machine:

- Tier off or unconfigured → an active repo syncs as on main.
- Tier on → **every** active repo, repo-enabled or globally tracked, needs
  `trust_all`, every configured origin URL's normalized key in
  `trusted_origins`, or (only when there is no origin) its canonical path in
  `trusted_paths`. Errors fail closed.

Consent is recorded three ways, all into the same file: `entire enable`
records it for the repo being enabled; the pre-push prompt offers **Yes**
(this repo / all clones of its origin), **Not now** (re-ask next push), and
**Always** (`trust_all`) — through the terminal, never Git's stdin, and never
implicitly in accessible mode; `entire trust [--revoke]` grants or withdraws
it. Revoke removes the repo's current origin keys and its current path; an
entry from a *previous* origin URL is not recognized and stays. A hold never
blocks the user's own push: the branch lands, checkpoint data stays local (the
refs backend keeps its queue), one stderr line explains, and the first trusted
push drains the backlog. Both egress entry points are gated
(`ManualCommitStrategy.prePush` and `PushQueuedCheckpointRefs`).

## Status and doctor

`entire status` prints the global-tracking line (on/off, agents covered, why
this repo is inactive) and the per-repo trust state; `--json` exposes
`global_tracking.{enabled, settings_path, activation_source, active_here,
inactive_reason, trust_state, trust_source, held_checkpoints}`. `entire doctor`
reports an unreadable user file, missing or unverifiable user-level hooks
(report-only — the post-run installs them), unusable exclude patterns, an
origin that cannot be normalized, a held repo, and a globally tracked repo
whose git hooks are absent (drift, deliberate `core.hooksPath` skip, or an
unresolvable hooks dir).

Key files: `settings/repopolicy/{types,policy,activation,repository,trust,user_settings}.go`,
`settings/{global,trust}.go`, `paths/invisible.go`, `hook_policy.go`,
`strategy/global_setup.go`, `strategy/trust_prompt.go`,
`strategy/manual_commit_push.go`, `global_warn.go`, `trust_cmd.go`,
`agent/user_hooks.go`, `agent/{claudecode,geminicli}/hooks_user.go`.

attachment.snippet:
1	# Global Tracking
2	
3	Global tracking lets Entire capture agent sessions in every git repository on
4	a machine without running `entire enable` in each one. It is configured only
5	in the user's settings file — there is no CLI flag that turns it on and no
6	wizard — and it is built from two inputs that already exist: the repository's
7	own `.entire/settings*.json` and the user's `~/.config/entire/settings.json`.
8	Nothing under `.git/` is a policy record; the only files Entire writes there
9	in global mode are runtime data and one stamp.
10	
11	## The settings file
12	
13	`~/.config/entire/settings.json` (or `$ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR/settings.json`) is
14	strict-decoded; an unknown key or malformed JSON turns the tier off machine-wide
15	(fail closed) and `entire doctor` says so.
16	
17	```json
18	{
19	  "global": {
20	    "enabled": true,
21	    "exclude_paths": ["~/scratch/**"],
22	    "exclude_paths_exact": ["~"],
23	    "exclude_origins": ["github.com/acme/private-*"],
24	    "trust_all": false,
25	    "trusted_origins": ["github.com/acme/widgets"],
26	    "trusted_paths": ["/Users/me/code/notes"]
27	  }
28	}
29	```
30	
31	- `enabled` — both `true` and `false` count as *configured*; an absent block is
32	  *unconfigured* (zero cost, no user-level hooks).
33	- `exclude_paths` — `~`-expanded doublestar globs against the worktree root (a
34	  bare directory pattern excludes its subtree). `exclude_paths_exact` matches
35	  one root only, no cascade — the way to exclude `$HOME` as a dotfiles repo
36	  without excluding everything under it. `exclude_origins` — globs against the
37	  origin URL normalized to `host/owner/repo`. An unusable pattern, or an origin
38	  that is present but cannot be normalized, deactivates the tier for that repo
39	  (fail closed).
40	- `trust_all`, `trusted_origins`, `trusted_paths` — checkpoint-egress consent
41	  (below). `entire trust` writes these; users may edit them by hand.
42	
43	## Activation (derived, never recorded)
44	
45	`repopolicy.ClassifyRepoPolicy` derives one `RepoPolicy` per process from the
46	repository's own settings files first and the user file second
47	(`cmd/entire/cli/settings/repopolicy/policy.go`):
48	
49	| Repo settings | User `global.enabled` | Result |
50	| --- | --- | --- |
51	| project `settings.json` (default enabled) or `settings.local.json` with an explicit `enabled` key | any | **Local** activation if enabled; an explicit `enabled: false` is a veto that also blocks the tier |
52	| none | `true`, repo not excluded | **Global** activation |
53	| none | `false`, absent, or repo excluded | inactive |
54	
55	This is main's `IsSetUpAndEnabled` contract for repo-enabled repos, with one
56	deliberate refinement: a `settings.local.json` written by an unrelated feature
57	(investigate config, …) without an `enabled` key does not pin a globally
58	tracked repo into local mode. Committed `.entire/settings.json` activates a
59	fresh clone exactly as it does today — consent for *egress* is a separate
60	question (below), so cloned content never opens the sync path by itself.
61	
62	Hooks classify once (`prepareHookPolicy`) and carry the snapshot on `ctx`; a
63	repo-enabled repo whose settings the full loader rejects (`ErrScannerConfig`)
64	stays inactive for hooks, as on main. Classification errors fail closed for
65	Entire's work and never fail the user's git or agent operation.
66	
67	## Runtime layout (a function of activation source)
68	
69	`RepoPolicy.RuntimeRoot()` decides where `.entire/{metadata,logs,tmp}` live:
70	
71	- **Local** → `<worktree>/.entire/…` (main's layout, unchanged).
72	- **Global** → `<git-common-dir>/entire/worktree/<worktree-hash>/…` — nothing in
73	  the checked-out tree, so `git status --porcelain` stays byte-clean; linked
74	  worktrees get separate roots.
75	
76	`paths.AbsPath` routes only those three prefixes; configuration
77	(`.entire/settings*.json`) always resolves to the literal worktree. A repo that
78	was captured globally and is later `entire enable`d switches to the worktree
79	layout for new activity; its earlier git-side runtime data is left in place
80	(no migration — `full.jsonl` is regenerated each Stop, and session state lives
81	in `.git/entire-sessions` regardless). `disable --uninstall` removes it.
82	
83	## Lazy per-repo setup
84	
85	The first hook in a globally tracked repo (`strategy.MaybeEnsureGlobalSetup`,
86	from both the agent-hook and git-hook routes) installs Entire's git hooks and
87	ensures the checkpoint metadata ref. Git-hook presence is re-checked on every
88	hook (a file read), so deleted or outdated hooks come back on the next
89	activity; the ref step is guarded by a `primary-ref-ready` stamp in the
90	runtime root. When `core.hooksPath` resolves inside the worktree (a committed
91	`.husky/`), the hooks half is skipped — global tracking never writes into the
92	checked-out tree; agent-side capture still works and `entire doctor` explains
93	it. Every failure logs at Debug and returns.
94	
95	## User-level agent hooks
96	
97	Claude Code (`~/.claude/settings.json`) and Gemini CLI
98	(`~/.gemini/settings.json`) support user-level hooks with the same inventory
99	and command form as the repo-level ones, so each agent deduplicates them.
100	`globalPostRun` (root `PersistentPostRun`, plus the installer) reconciles them
101	against the tier on every foreground `entire` command: installed while
102	`global.enabled` is true for agents present on the machine, removed when the
103	tier is configured but off, untouched while unconfigured. That is how a hand
104	edit of the settings file takes effect without a dedicated command. Hook
105	processes are hidden commands and never reconcile.
106	
107	## Checkpoint egress and trust
108	
109	`settings.CheckpointEgressAllowed` (`repopolicy.DecideEgress`) is the single
110	predicate for whether checkpoint data may leave the machine:
111	
112	- Tier off or unconfigured → an active repo syncs as on main.
113	- Tier on → **every** active repo, repo-enabled or globally tracked, needs
114	  `trust_all`, every configured origin URL's normalized key in
115	  `trusted_origins`, or (only when there is no origin) its canonical path in
116	  `trusted_paths`. Errors fail closed.
117	
118	Consent is recorded three ways, all into the same file: `entire enable`
119	records it for the repo being enabled; the pre-push prompt offers **Yes**
120	(this repo / all clones of its origin), **Not now** (re-ask next push), and
121	**Always** (`trust_all`) — through the terminal, never Git's stdin, and never
122	implicitly in accessible mode; `entire trust [--revoke]` grants or withdraws
123	it. Revoke removes the repo's current origin keys and its current path; an
124	entry from a *previous* origin URL is not recognized and stays. A hold never
125	blocks the user's own push: the branch lands, checkpoint data stays local (the
126	refs backend keeps its queue), one stderr line explains, and the first trusted
127	push drains the backlog. Both egress entry points are gated
128	(`ManualCommitStrategy.prePush` and `PushQueuedCheckpointRefs`).
129	
130	## Status and doctor
131	
132	`entire status` prints the global-tracking line (on/off, agents covered, why
133	this repo is inactive) and the per-repo trust state; `--json` exposes
134	`global_tracking.{enabled, settings_path, activation_source, active_here,
135	inactive_reason, trust_state, trust_source, held_checkpoints}`. `entire doctor`
136	reports an unreadable user file, missing or unverifiable user-level hooks
137	(report-only — the post-run installs them), unusable exclude patterns, an
138	origin that cannot be normalized, a held repo, and a globally tracked repo
139	whose git hooks are absent (drift, deliberate `core.hooksPath` skip, or an
140	unresolvable hooks dir).
141	
142	Key files: `settings/repopolicy/{types,policy,activation,repository,trust,user_settings}.go`,
143	`settings/{global,trust}.go`, `paths/invisible.go`, `hook_policy.go`,
144	`strategy/global_setup.go`, `strategy/trust_prompt.go`,
145	`strategy/manual_commit_push.go`, `global_warn.go`, `trust_cmd.go`,
146	`agent/user_hooks.go`, `agent/{claudecode,geminicli}/hooks_user.go`.
